title: Cognitive Offloading
summary: External tools and actions can alter the processing demands of a task. H1 can be read as an engineered offloading system whose causal status is then tested.

title: The Extended Mind
summary: A classic argument about reliably integrated external resources. H1 separates availability, integration, and epistemic authority rather than assuming they are the same.

title: Source Monitoring
summary: Remembering content and judging its origin are separable. E08 creates a synthetic provenance task without assuming human-like mechanisms.

title: How Do We Know That We Know?
summary: Metacognitive confidence can follow accessible cues. E09 therefore requires a matched observer predicting the same target decision.

title: Lost in the Middle
summary: Long-context models do not use all context positions uniformly. This motivates compact state as an access and cost tool even when raw history contains more information.

title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
summary: An operating-system-inspired memory manager for LLMs. It is a neighboring engineering idea: external memory can extend behavior without being native hidden recurrence.

title: Prompt Injection as Role Confusion
summary: The paper argues that models infer roles from how text is written, not only where it comes from. That is closely adjacent to E08 narrative-over-metadata and the E08c role counterbalance.

title: Emergent Introspective Awareness in Large Language Models
summary: Activation-intervention work tests whether models can report injected internal concepts and prior intentions. H1 does not make those latent-state claims; the paper helps locate the H2 boundary.

title: Memory Provenance Laundering in LLM Agents
summary: Recent agent-memory work highlights how consolidation can preserve action triggers while losing low-trust provenance. This is an applied systems cousin of H1 source-ledger concerns.
